why: Issue #930, and this is the SHIPPED defect restored rather than an invented one. `.hud-damage` rests at `opacity: 0` and `@keyframes hud-damage-flash` ramps opacity and nothing else, so cancelling the animation leaves the vignette at 0 forever. Measured on the stylesheet in a browser, twelve samples over 480ms after the class toggle `hud.ts` performs: peak opacity 1.00 with motion allowed, 0 under reduced motion. The old two-class list named `.hud-capacity--flash` and `.hud-count--pop` only, so this state passed the suite for as long as it stood.
killedBy: hud.css: every animation answers to the resolved motion policy (issue #631) never answers an animation by cancelling a cue that rests invisible
